summary:
Our project is an interactive 3D Solar System application that allows users to explore the machines and equipment left behind during humanity's space exploration missions.

Users can observe the Solar System from a distant perspective and interact with different celestial bodies to discover the stories of abandoned spacecraft, rovers, and scientific equipment, mainly on the Moon and Mars, with a few examples from other worlds.

The application addresses NASA's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by turning space exploration history into an engaging and interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading about these machines, users can explore their locations, missions, purposes, and scientific contributions.

This project is important because these machines represent humanity's curiosity, innovation, and determination to explore the unknown. Although some missions have ended, their contributions to science should never be forgotten.
details:
Overview & How It Works: Our project is an interactive 3D Solar System web application and digital memorial dedicated to humanity's retired, stranded, and sacrificed space exploration machines. Built using WebGL and Three.js, the application renders a photorealistic 3D model of the Sun and the eight planets, complete with orbital mechanics, particle-based solar flares, atmospheric glows, and glowing orbital trails. Users can freely navigate the cosmos, zoom in on any planet or the Moon, and click on celestial bodies to smoothly transition the camera into orbit around them. Upon focusing on a planet, an interactive UI drawer opens, displaying official NASA planetary fact sheets alongside profiles of iconic abandoned spacecraft and rovers (such as Apollo 11's Eagle, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Cassini-Huygens, Galileo, MESSENGER, Magellan, and Voyager 2). Each machine profile includes its mission status, exact resting coordinates, historical imagery, and a first-person narrative telling its story. Furthermore, users can write and transmit personalized "Tribute Messages" to the resting coordinates of these machines.

Benefits & Intended Impact: Space exploration data is often presented in static tables or disconnected archives. Our project bridges the gap between raw astronomical data and human emotion. By combining accurate planetary metrics with storytelling, it transforms cold hardware into relatable pioneers of human curiosity. The intended impact is to inspire students, educators, and space enthusiasts to appreciate both the scientific achievements and the enduring legacy of robotic explorers that paved the way for human spaceflight.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
  • 3D Graphics & Post-Processing: Three.js (r128) utilizing OrbitControls, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass for realistic solar and atmospheric glow, custom HTML5 Canvas procedural textures, and particle systems.
  • UI/UX & Styling: Tailwind CSS, Font Awesome icons, and Web Audio API for ambient space acoustics.
  • Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) with Live Server.

Creativity & Design Considerations:

  • Emotional Storytelling: Instead of merely listing technical specs, we gave each rover and probe a "voice" through first-person memoirs (e.g., Opportunity's final message before the dust storm), creating a poignant digital monument.
  • Resilience & Performance: We engineered a hybrid rendering pipeline that combines high-resolution planetary textures with intelligent procedural HTML5 Canvas fallbacks and GPU-accelerated particle systems, ensuring smooth 60 FPS performance across standard laptops without requiring heavy installations.
  • Accessibility & Localization: Recognizing a global audience, we built a real-time bilingual toggle (English and Vietnamese), intuitive mouse/touch navigation, and a clean glassmorphism UI that keeps the focus on the 3D cosmos.
